profiles.name: PartUsage
profiles.purpose: Describes a system or system part in a context. A definition describes its kind; multiple usages can share that kind.
learning_points: A referential part remains a PartUsage. It is not converted into the metaclass ReferenceUsage just because its declaration contains ref.
Owning a part declaration, featuring its values, and making those values composite are separate mechanisms.
The declared partDefinition property has multiplicity 0..*. Class-level constraints still require at least one applicable PartDefinition typing; declaration cardinality alone is not the whole rule.
The normalized defaults below describe metamodel fields. The multiplicity and composition of a part in a user model follow contextual SysML rules.
profiles.example_focus: wheel is a composite part usage within Assembly. spare is an owned but referential part usage. Both are typed by Wheel; the [0..1] on spare explicitly constrains its modeled values.

relationships.description: A part usage has applicable part-definition typing, explicit or supplied through its semantic specialization.
relationships.condition: Do not restrict every allowed explicit type to PartDefinition; the source also permits qualifying item definitions and kernel structures.

relationships.description: A part usage can declare nested part usages as features in its context.
relationships.condition: Permitted examples do not establish that every nesting is valid; membership, featuring and composition constraints still apply.

relationships.description: Ports can be declared within a part usage or its defining type.
relationships.condition: The port typing and context-specific referentiality rules apply independently of the enclosing part.

notations.title: Composite and referential part usages
notations.description: Rounded rectangle with a part usage label. The referential variant has a dashed outline and the ref prefix. Compartments and side ports are additional variants.

caveats: The examples have been checked against source notation, but no SysML parser or semantic engine was run.
No exhaustive permission matrix or complete notation grammar is claimed.

profiles.name: PartDefinition
profiles.purpose: Defines a reusable kind of system or system part, including features that usages of that kind can have.
learning_points: A definition is a classifier; a part usage is a feature in context. They retain different metaclass identities.
Declaring a nested definition introduces a scoped kind. It does not by itself declare a part usage.
Properties of this metaclass describe the language definition, rather than arbitrary attributes such as a modeled wheel diameter.
profiles.example_focus: Wheel, Axle and Assembly are part definitions. Their port and part declarations specify features; assembly : Assembly is a separate usage of the defined kind.

relationships.description: Part usages can use the kind introduced by a part definition.
relationships.condition: Typing is distinct from model ownership; many usages can share the same definition.

relationships.description: A part definition can declare port usages as features.
relationships.condition: Port definitions determine permitted port typing; the enclosing declaration is not a substitute for that type.

notations.title: Part definition node
notations.context: Definition node in a structural view
notations.description: Sharp-corner rectangle with the part def keyword and definition name. Compartment and interconnection contents may extend the basic node.

caveats: Instance-level composition is governed by usages and their context, rather than by the outline of the definition box.

profiles.name: PortUsage
profiles.purpose: Describes an interaction point in a structural context, typed by a port definition.
learning_points: A port usage can appear as a full node or as a small boundary glyph; its semantic identity is not determined by the drawing size.
Only port definitions can type a port usage. Conjugated typing uses ~ and reverses in/out while preserving inout.
The source overview and well-formedness constraints need to be read together: nested-port exceptions prevent an unconditional rule that every nested port value must be non-composite.
A connection referencing a port does not by itself establish a flow or an executable transfer.
profiles.example_focus: hub and mount are port usages typed by Mount. The connection refers to them through axle.mount and wheel.hub. The example uses no directional arrows or transfer behavior.

relationships.description: Port usages can be declared in part definitions.
relationships.condition: Type featuring, declaration ownership and referentiality remain separate questions.

relationships.description: Port usages can be nested in part usages.
relationships.condition: Nesting is contextual; a glyph placed on a boundary is not itself evidence of a new ownership rule.

relationships.description: A connection can reference a port feature as an end target.
relationships.condition: Preserve end roles and reference-subsetting relationships; do not infer flow semantics from the line.

notations.title: Full node and boundary port
notations.description: The full node is rounded and labeled port. The compact outline in this older illustration is a geometry primitive only: displayed boundary alternatives include horizontal or vertical direction indicators, plus side-specific labels. Their selection and layout are separate renderer responsibilities.

notations.title: Restricted reference and proxy variants
notations.context: Nested ports and part usages within interconnection views
notations.description: Dotted-outline reference port productions are restricted to nested ports. The filled-dot proxy option is restricted to a part usage contained within an interconnection view.

caveats: The pinned XMI overview overgeneralizes referentiality; the profile preserves the nested-port qualification rather than silently applying that overview as an unconditional rule.

profiles.name: ConnectionUsage
profiles.purpose: Represents a structural connection with end features. It combines PartUsage and ConnectorAsUsage semantics and retains its own model-element identity.
learning_points: A connection is a model element with end roles and references, even when drawn as a simple line.
Nonabstract connections require at least two ends. Each end is referential with multiplicity 1..1; cross multiplicity is a separate concept.
Allowed typing includes connection definitions and suitable KerML association structures.
A structural connection is not interchangeable with a binding, succession or flow.
profiles.example_focus: link is a named binary connection. Its ends refer to axle.mount and wheel.hub. The plain solid line is an illustrative connection representation, with no flow direction implied.

relationships.description: ConnectionUsage directly specializes PartUsage as well as ConnectorAsUsage.
relationships.condition: A connection therefore has inherited part properties, but adds connector end structure and applicable constraints.

relationships.description: The example connects two port usages through qualified feature paths.
relationships.condition: Retain the connection end declarations and their reference-subsetting semantics, rather than storing only a graphical line.

notations.title: Binary edge and connection node
notations.description: A connection can use a solid binary line with an optional label, or a rounded full node labeled connection. The example omits the optional direction-indication arrow.

notations.title: N-ary connection variant
notations.context: Connections with more than two ends
notations.description: The grammar also provides a central filled dot with segments to the connected usage nodes. It is an additional representation, not a universal replacement for binary lines.

caveats: This profile illustrates selected structural notations and does not implement execution or all association-structure semantics.
